absent: Packet header layouts, verb encodings, and handshake message sequences for query, control, close, and establish exchange.
Internals of packet transport helpers including get packet, send packet, send close, start handshake, library open, and library character IO.
Firmware semantics and error codes for OPAL character IO and flush, SBI console and debug console, RTAS terminal calls, VIO character IO, and generic udbg hooks.
Synchronization and ownership for established flag, modem cache, and update flag, and interaction with reader thread beyond opened handling.
Complete VIO probe allocation path, driver registration, and interrupt mapping beyond truncated fragment.
Timing guarantees, retry limits in milliseconds, and console versus tty hangup propagation through hvc core and notifier helpers.

findings.text: Establishment exposes a blocking bringup that succeeds only when an established indicator becomes true within bounded polling. It tolerates a pending inbound packet, otherwise forces closure and handshake restart with a second longer bound. Success implies subsequent modem query and local DTR assertion before publication of an opened indicator that enables reads; timeout leaves opened unpublished.

Lifecycle states are unestablished, handshake in progress, established with modem valid, and opened for IO, plus closed. Transitions allow early exit when already established, forced close plus restart on initial timeout, and failure return when handshake never completes. Close transitions differ by console flag: console retains link state while non-console clears opened, conditionally clears DTR, and tears down link; both release tty association.

Modem control query publishes an update expectation, emits a query packet, then waits bounded time for completion; link loss during wait fails distinct from timeout. DTR update is conditional: cached value comparison suppresses redundant transmission, otherwise cache is updated and a masked control packet reflecting asserted or cleared DTR is emitted with send status propagated.

Close and init define ownership. Init zeroes state and records inbound and outbound callbacks with terminal identity and console marker. Close for non-console clears opened under synchronization, clears DTR when no tty is attached or hangup on close is configured, and issues link teardown; console close omits teardown. Both paths drop tty reference and clear pointer.
Delay helper preserves early boot safety by selecting busy wait when interrupts are disabled and sleeping wait otherwise for the same requested duration.

Opened flag mutation on close is serialized with the hvc instance lock using irq save and restore to coordinate with the reader thread, while bringup publishes opened after a write barrier once handshake polling has observed establishment. Per-terminal raw receive buffering serializes refill, quirk filtering, and consume under a dedicated buffer lock with irq save and restore.

Per-terminal state comprises a firmware terminal number, a protocol selector distinguishing raw from packet mode, embedded packet-mode state, a buffer lock, a fixed-size receive area with remaining length and read offset. A global table indexed by virtual terminal number holds pointers with index zero reserved for early console backed by a static instance.

Character operation tables bind protocol to callbacks. OPAL packet table carries receive, transmit, flush, open, close, hangup, and modem query and update. VIO raw table carries receive, transmit, and generic irq notifier hooks; VIO packet table carries packet receive and transmit with packet open, close, hangup, and modem query and update. SBI legacy, SBI debug console, RTAS, and UDBG tables carry only receive and transmit.

OPAL platform handling selects protocol from compatible property, derives terminal number from address property with zero default, reuses boot storage for the boot terminal or allocates fresh storage and for packet mode initializes library with atomic transmit, establishes equal virtual and firmware index mapping, resolves interrupt with event fallback, allocates endpoint, and marks sharing. Removal frees non-boot storage and clears slot. Platform driver binds probe and remove with match table. Early discovery prefers chosen stdout with legacy path fallback, bounds-checks index, records boot storage, initializes and establishes packet console immediately when selected, installs low-level hooks, registers preferred console, and instantiates mapping.

RISC-V backend prefers block debug console when firmware reports availability, else legacy per-character console when configured, else reports absence of device. Both enabled paths allocate endpoint zero with depth 256 and instantiate zero to zero. Legacy receive stops at first negative firmware result; legacy transmit forwards each byte; debug console paths forward whole buffers to firmware block calls.

RTAS backend resolves put and get firmware tokens during both console setup and driver setup and fails when either remains unknown. Console setup instantiates a fixed cookie to index zero and registers preferred console; driver setup allocates the same cookie with depth 16 and records endpoint in a driver global. Transmit and receive loop per byte and stop early on firmware error, returning count transferred.

UDBG bridge requires a low-level output hook for both console setup and driver setup, otherwise reports absence of device. Both use index zero, allocate with depth 16 and record endpoint in a driver global, instantiate zero to zero, and register preferred console on console path. Output iterates while hook remains present; input returns zero when poll hook absent and otherwise copies until poll signals no data.

VIO raw receive refills only when empty by fetching into per-terminal storage, filters a firmware quirk, then satisfies the request up to available bytes while advancing offset and decrementing remainder. Raw transmit forwards directly. Packet receive and transmit delegate to shared library after validating terminal slot. Packet open registers irq notification before library open and propagates registration failure; packet close and hangup invoke library close before irq removal or hangup notification.

Modem cache reads return stored value and fail when terminal storage is missing. Updates affect only DTR, with set taking precedence over clear, and delegate to shared write routine. OPAL close and hangup first invoke shared close then delegate to irq removal or hangup notification.

Raw path must strip a zero byte following carriage return to hide firmware behavior. Packet transmit must use an atomic firmware put to avoid interleaving packet bytes. Early output must retry when firmware reports no progress or busy and, for OPAL, flush console each attempt. VIO early output must bounce through a sixteen-byte area because raw transmit requires that minimum. Duplicate terminal numbers and unrecognized protocols must be rejected during probe.

Low-level poll signals absence with a negative sentinel and blocking input spins until data arrives; VIO variant also reports absence when early storage is missing and otherwise spins with a delay loop. Newline output is expanded with carriage return. Dispatch selects raw or packet low-level routines according to boot protocol. Debug early entries bind a configured index to boot storage and install hooks, with packet variant additionally initializing as console and establishing immediately.
RTAS console is identified by fixed value 0x67781e15 paired with console index zero for both instantiation and allocation.

VIO driver is named hvc_console and matches serial hvterm1 for raw mode and serial hvterm-protocol for packet mode. OPAL distinguishes ibm,opal-console-raw for raw mode and ibm,opal-console-hvsi for packet mode during both probe and early discovery.

VIO probe validates parameters, selects raw or packet protocol from compatible property with error on unknown, and detects boot instance by matching unit address against boot terminal number to reuse index zero, otherwise scans for a free slot.
